subject: Cost checks & MAP parachute plan - batching/caching sensitivity
messages:
From: David Kim <david.kim@redwoodinference.com>
To: Michael Carter <michael.carter@cobaltanalytics.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwoodinference.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-12-01T09:14:00Z
Subject: Cost checks & MAP parachute plan - batching/caching sensitivity

Hi Michael —

Thanks again for taking time today. Per our call I wanted to kick off a lightweight MAP thread focused specifically on the unit-econ checks (tokens/$), caching and batching assumptions, and a small "parachute" cost plan you can fall back to if early unit economics look worse than expected.

Quick asks to get us started:
- Can you confirm expected daily active users and average queries per session (ballpark fine) and the 95th percentile query size in tokens?
- Any caching opportunities in your flow (pre-filled forms, repeated prompts, or canonical responses)?
- Which latency SLO matters most for the use case (p95 < 300ms, p95 < 800ms, etc.)?

We'll draft a MAP addendum that includes: an acceptance gate (tokens/$ threshold), evaluation plan (sample prompts, holdout set), rollout timeline, and a parachute configuration (quantized model + aggressive prefix caching + larger batching window).

I'll circulate a first-pass spreadsheet by EOD Friday; Laura will own the token model sensitivity analysis.

Thanks,
David Kim
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
---

Subject: Re: Cost checks & MAP parachute plan - batching/caching sensitivity

Thanks David. Good plan.

Answers in brief:
- Expected DAUs for phase 1: 8k–12k; we estimate ~1.8 queries per session. Peak concurrency unknown but we can share hourly traffic soon.
- Typical prompt sizes: median ~150 tokens, 95th ~620 tokens (these are estimates from our analytics).
- Caching: we have ~12% repeat prompt rate at the surface level (same input from returning users). There are a few canonical responses for onboarding flows which should be cacheable.
- Latency SLO: p95 target is 500ms — anything higher will push stakeholders to consider async UX.

Procurement is mainly worried about tokens/$ sensitivity. Sarah (cc) will coordinate the legal/finance Qs; she asked if we can provide a conservative worst-case cost scenario and a cheaper fallback that keeps product usable.

Michael
VP Product, Cobalt Analytics

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwoodinference.com>
To: David Kim <david.kim@redwoodinference.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwoodinference.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-12-03T10:05:00Z
Subject: RE: Cost checks & MAP parachute plan - batching/caching sensitivity

All — drafting the MAP addendum now. Moving internal checklist into the thread so we have a shared audit trail. Proposed gates and evaluation steps (first pass):

1) Acceptance gates (must pass to go GA):
   - Baseline tokens/$ <= $0.0065 per request (based on expected prompt distribution and default model).
   - Cache hit rate >= 18% on canonical flows (reduces token spend by ~10–15%).
   - p95 latency <= 600ms on baseline config.

2) Evaluation plan (week 0–4):
   - Week 0: collect 7 days of real traffic sample; identify top 50 prompts and token-size distribution.
   - Week 1: run offline token-modeling (attached will be a spreadsheet) with 3 model variants (fp16, int8 quant, int4 aggressive).
   - Week 2: run a canary with 5% traffic using caching-first route (prefetch + KV cache) to validate hit rate assumptions.
   - Week 3–4: ramp to 25% then 50% contingent on cost and latency gates.

3) Parachute plan (if base gates fail):
   - Immediate switch to quantized int8 variant + increase batch window by 50% (accept slight p95 increase) AND enable TTL-based answer caching for canonical prompts.
   - Add fallback route to a cheaper open-model for non-critical flows (rerouting rules in MAP).

Open items for the MAP doc:
- Final tokens per request distribution from Cobalt (Michael/Sarah)
- Stakeholder threshold for max monthly spend (procurement)
- Who signs off on parachute activation (suggest: Cobalt product lead + Redwood AE)

I'll attach the sensitivity workbook (token_modeling_cobalt.csv) and an initial MAP workbook (Cobalt_MAP_v2.xlsx) for your review. Ben, can you run the preflight throughput test on Thursday? Neha, can you draft the acceptance gate language for the MAP addendum?

Thanks,
Laura Bennett
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

Attachments referenced: token_modeling_cobalt.csv, Cobalt_MAP_v2.xlsx

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwoodinference.com>

Date: 2026-12-07T11:33:00Z
Subject: RE: Cost checks & MAP parachute plan - batching/caching sensitivity

Laura — happy to run the preflight. I have a lightweight script that will replay 48hrs of sampled traffic and report per-token costs across model variants and batching windows.

Plan: run baseline (no quant, batch=8, cache off), then int8 (batch=8), then int8 (batch=12), then int4 (batch=12) and capture p50/p95 latency + tokens per dollar. I can post results to the MAP workbook and flag any scenario where tokens/$ exceeds $0.0075 (high risk).

Will start Thurs morning and share a short readout by Friday.

- Ben
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

Attachment: preflight_script_v1.sh (referenced)

Subject: RE: Cost checks & MAP parachute plan - batching/caching sensitivity

Michael / Sarah —

Attached is the first-pass MAP addendum and the token sensitivity workbook: Cobalt_MAP_v2.xlsx and token_modeling_cobalt.csv. Highlights:
- With your supplied median/95th token sizes, baseline (fp16, batch=8) estimates ~ $0.0058 per request — under our baseline gate.
- If cache hit rate drops below 10% we breach $0.0075 in the worst-case traffic spike; Ben's preflight will validate.
- Parachute plan (int8 + batch=12 + aggressive TTL caching) drops worst-case cost to ~$0.0039 per request but increases p95 by ~150–220ms in our simulated runs.

Next steps:
1) Sarah — can you confirm max acceptable monthly spend or soft cap? Procurement asked for that number to finalize billing terms.
2) Michael — please share a 14-day traffic export (anonymized) so we can run the full sensitivity in the workbook.
3) We'll schedule a 30min sync next Tuesday to walk the MAP gates and parachute activation checklist.

Thanks and happy to adjust the MAP language per procurement's requirements.

-David
